name: Boston
summary: The trip's opening act — colonial history, a ballgame, and chowder.
seasonalTip: Arrive late September for a Red Sox game before the season ends.

lodging.name: The Omni Parker House
lodging.blurb: Oldest continuously operating hotel in the U.S.; birthplace of the Boston cream pie.

foodMustTry.name: Clam chowder at Union Oyster House
foodMustTry.blurb: America's oldest restaurant; the New England classic done right.

foodMustTry.name: A cannoli in the North End
foodMustTry.blurb: Mike's or Modern — pick a side, then eat one from each and decide for yourself.

days.label: Day 1 — Freedom Trail & Fenway
days.summary: History by day, a ballgame by night.

item.title: Walk the Freedom Trail
item.blurb: A 2.5-mile red line through 16 colonial-era sites — the essential Boston primer, and the best possible first walk of the entire trip.

item.title: Chowder at Union Oyster House
item.blurb: Open since 1826 and sitting right on the Freedom Trail. Sit at the raw bar, order the chowder, keep moving.

item.title: Wander the North End
item.blurb: Boston's Italian quarter: narrow streets, Paul Revere's house, and the cannoli argument you're about to settle.

item.title: Red Sox game at Fenway Park
item.blurb: The oldest ballpark in the majors — catch the season before it closes in early October.

days.label: Day 2 — Museums & the Charles
days.summary: One great museum, one great river, one crossing into Cambridge.

item.title: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum
item.blurb: A Venetian palazzo built around a courtyard — and the site of the largest unsolved art heist in history. The empty frames still hang where the stolen paintings were.

item.title: Walk the Charles River Esplanade to Cambridge
item.blurb: The city's front lawn: sailboats, skyline, and the bridge across to Harvard Square.

item.title: Dinner and bookstores in Harvard Square
item.blurb: Street musicians, the Harvard Book Store's basement, and dinner somewhere loud and cheap.

days.label: Day 3 — Free Day
days.summary: Breathe. Sleep in, wander, catch up on laundry and life. Nothing here is required.

freeMenu.title: Samuel Adams Brewery tour
freeMenu.blurb: If you feel like it — a low-key tasting in Jamaica Plain.

freeMenu.title: USS Constitution
freeMenu.blurb: "Old Ironsides" — the oldest commissioned warship afloat, still crewed by the Navy.

days.label: Day 4 — Drive to Portland, Maine
days.summary: Short coastal hop north. Take the slow road.

commute.scenicNote: Coastal Route 1 adds an hour but trades the highway for lighthouses, clam shacks, and the first real taste of Maine.

stopsAlongWay.title: Nubble Lighthouse, York
stopsAlongWay.blurb: One of the most photographed lighthouses in the country, sitting on its own tiny island.

stopsAlongWay.title: Bob's Clam Hut, Kittery
stopsAlongWay.blurb: Fried clams at the Maine state line since 1956. This is lunch.
